name: Graphify
attribution_status: Not attributable to any source post. Identified during related research.
intended_use: Use for turning a codebase, plus its docs, PDFs, images and media, into a local knowledge graph that coding agents query instead of grepping files.
supported_agents: Any MCP client (graphify-mcp or hosted Graphify Cloud MCP)
runtime_requirements: Python 3.11.5-3.14 with uv (recommended) or pipx. Optional extras add PDF, Office, video/audio (faster-whisper + yt-dlp), MCP server, Leiden clustering, Ollama/OpenAI/Gemini/Anthropic/Bedrock backends, SQL/Postgres, Neo4j/FalkorDB push.

hardware.notes: Code parsing is tree-sitter on the CPU with no model. The optional local video/audio transcription (faster-whisper) has no documented hardware needs. No GPU requirement is documented.

installation:
uv tool install graphifyy
graphify install
# alternatives: pipx install graphifyy | pip install graphifyy
configuration: `graphify install` (or `graphify <platform> install`, `--project`, `--strict`) registers the skill and hooks or instruction files for the chosen assistant. A `.graphifyrc` in the scan root sets per-project options (language for ambiguous extensions, query_budget, query_depth, viz_node_limit); backends and logging are set with environment variables such as GRAPHIFY_BACKEND.
inputs: Source code in about 40 languages (tree-sitter AST)
SQL schemas and live PostgreSQL via --postgres DSN
credentials_required: None for code-only graphs. The semantic pass over docs, PDFs and images uses the assistant's own model inside /graphify; headless `graphify extract` needs one of GEMINI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_API_KEY, MOONSHOT_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, Azure OpenAI key+endpoint, AWS IAM (Bedrock), a local Ollama, or the `claude` CLI. The hosted Graphify Cloud MCP needs a Graphify account.
commercial_use_notes: Apache-2.0 allows commercial use, modification and redistribution with notice and patent terms. The 'graphify' name and logo are marks of Graphify Labs; community projects using the name must say they are not affiliated. Graphify Cloud is a separate hosted commercial service.
integration_notes: No native integration with catalogue peers is asserted. Examples using another tool are proposed handoffs.
conflicts: Skip when a small repo is easier to grep, or when docs must not reach any cloud model and you cannot use Ollama or --code-only.

Its Claude Code hooks fire before Read/Grep/Glob and Bash readers; with --strict they deny Read/Grep once per session until a graph query. This can clash with other PreToolUse Read hooks, such as claude-mem's file-read gate.
Without the `leiden` extra, clustering silently falls back to networkx Louvain; switching later reshuffles every community and needs a full relabel.
security_notes: The official PyPI package is `graphifyy` (double y); the README warns other graphify* packages are not affiliated (typosquat risk).
Install writes hooks or always-on instruction files (AGENTS.md, .cursor/rules, CODEBUDDY.md) into assistant config; `graphify uninstall` removes them.
`graphify add <url>` fetches remote papers and videos (yt-dlp) into the graph.
The Pi guard hook fails open and needs graphify on an absolute PATH entry outside the project.
privacy_notes: Code is parsed locally; README: nothing leaves the machine for code, and `graphify extract` runs offline for code-only corpora.

Docs, PDFs and images go to the assistant's model or to the configured API provider; auto-detection order is Gemini, Kimi, Claude, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Azure, Bedrock, Ollama. Kimi routes to Moonshot AI servers in China. GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none or ollama keeps everything local.
No telemetry or analytics per README.
Every query/path/explain call (including the question text) is logged to ~/.cache/graphify-queries.log by default; set GRAPHIFY_QUERY_LOG_DISABLE=1 to opt out.
Connecting to the hosted MCP at api.graphify.com means the graph is served from Graphify Cloud, not your machine.
craft_notes: Best at structural code questions: tree-sitter resolves calls/imports/inherits across about 40 languages and every edge is tagged EXTRACTED or INFERRED, so `graphify path` reports a path's confidence as that of its weakest hop.
graph.html renders up to 5,000 nodes before switching to an aggregated community view; community labeling sends 100 communities per call, sized for about a 16k-token context.
Ambiguous extensions (.inc, .h, .m) can parse as the wrong language and yield a sparse but plausible-looking graph unless declared in .graphifyrc.

examples.independent: Run `/graphify .` in a repo, then `graphify path "UserService" "DatabasePool"` to trace how two components connect.
examples.combined: Proposed handoff: build a graphify graph of an existing repo, then give GRAPH_REPORT.md to spec-kit's /speckit-plan so the plan names real components and dependencies.

name: Spec Kit

specify init my-project --integration copilot
cd my-project

outputs: Generated agent commands or SKILL.md files

integration_notes: No native integration with catalogue peers is asserted. Examples using another tool are proposed handoffs.

name: Claude Mem
attribution_status: Not attributable to any source post. Identified during related research.
intended_use: Use for giving a coding agent persistent memory: hooks record each session's tool activity, an observer model compresses it into observations, and later sessions start with a compact index of them.
supported_agents: Copilot CLI, Goose, Roo Code, Warp, Zed (search only, sessions not recorded)
